record.paper_title: Fair Division under Joint Ownership: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Joint production under ELB and population monotonicity
record.original_question: In the one-input joint-production problem with a convex production set and arbitrary convex and monotonic preferences, does there exist a Pareto optimal mechanism satisfying both the Egalitarian Lower Bound and Population Monotonicity? Here the Egalitarian Lower Bound requires each agent's final welfare to be at least that agent's unanimity welfare, namely the welfare the agent could secure from a one-nth share of the production set if all agents had that same preference, and Population Monotonicity requires that when more agents appear to share the technology, the pre-existing population does not become better off.

The second notion of fairness is the analog of Equal Split Guarantee. In a nutshell it gives to each agent a claim on his (1/n)-th share of the production set.
As more agents appear to share the technology f, the initial population as a whole suffers a loss.

In both questions we assume arbitrary convex and monotonic preferences.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a one-input joint-production economy with a finite set $N=\{1,\dots,n\}$ of agents. There is a single input (e.g., labor) and a single output, with a production technology described by a convex production set $f$ (so the output $y$ produced from total input $x\ge 0$ satisfies a standard convexity assumption, e.g., $y\le f(x)$ with $f$ concave, nondecreasing, and $f(0)=0$). Each agent $i\in N$ has a preference relation $R_i$ over pairs (own input contribution, own output share) that is convex and monotonic (decreasing in own input, increasing in own output).

A mechanism associates to every economy $(N,f,(R_i)_{i\in N})$ an allocation specifying, for every agent, an input contribution and an output share that is feasible with respect to $f$. Define:

(i) Pareto Optimality: the chosen allocation is not Pareto-dominated by any other feasible allocation given the agents' preferences.

(ii) Egalitarian Lower Bound (ELB): for every profile $(R_1,\dots,R_n)$ and every agent $i$, the welfare of $i$ at the chosen allocation is at least the unanimity welfare of $i$, defined as the welfare $i$ would obtain by optimally exploiting the rescaled production set $\tfrac{1}{n}f$ (the $1/n$-share of the technology) under preference $R_i$ alone — equivalently, the welfare $i$ would secure if all $n$ agents had preference $R_i$ and the symmetric Pareto efficient outcome were chosen.

(iii) Population Monotonicity (PM): if a new agent joins the economy (so the set of agents grows from $N$ to $N\cup\{n+1\}$ with the technology $f$ unchanged), then no agent in the original population $N$ is strictly better off in the new allocation than in the original one.

Question: Does there exist a mechanism, defined on the domain of all such one-input joint-production problems with convex production set and arbitrary convex monotonic preferences, that simultaneously satisfies Pareto Optimality, the Egalitarian Lower Bound, and Population Monotonicity?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches on the compatibility of Pareto optimality, the Egalitarian Lower Bound, and Population Monotonicity in one-input joint-production problems with convex production sets did not turn up a definitive resolution. Related results exist on Leontief preferences, on TU games (Dutta–Ray egalitarian solution and population-monotonic allocation schemes for convex games), and on indivisible-good mechanisms with welfare lower bounds, but none directly settles the question for the general convex-production / convex-monotonic-preference domain. Status appears to remain open, but no authoritative confirmation was found.

status_evidence.title: Population monotonicity and egalitarianism
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies the maximal domain of TU games on which population monotonicity and egalitarian core selection are compatible (class of games with an egalitarian population monotonic allocation scheme).
status_evidence.claim: Related results characterize compatibility of egalitarianism and population monotonicity in TU games but do not settle the joint-production mechanism question.

status_evidence.title: Population monotonic and strategy-proof mechanisms respecting welfare lower bounds
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes population monotonic and incentive compatible mechanisms allocating an indivisible good efficiently subject to a welfare lower bound.
status_evidence.claim: Addresses related compatibility issues for indivisible goods with transfers, not the convex joint-production setting.

status_evidence.title: Egalitarian division under Leontief preferences
status_evidence.snippet: Studies egalitarian-equivalent allocations in joint-production problems restricted to Leontief preferences.
status_evidence.claim: Provides positive results in a restricted preference domain but does not resolve the general convex-preference case.
